liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Shakedown Street** (1 review): Opened the show with a funky version, and the band played relentlessly without letting up [6]
- **Easy Answers** (1 review): Described as beautiful and closing the first set [6]
- **Days Between** (1 review): Called killer in the second set, which ended with a rollicking U.S. Blues [6]

## Setlist highlights

- **Easy Answers**: rare: 9 archived performances [9]
- **A Love Supreme Jam**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [9]

## The recordings

- **deadandcompany2018-06-15.neumann_skm150.sunboy.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 20 songs; 175 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **DeadCo2018-06-15.DeadCo2018-06-15.flac16**: audience recording; 19 songs; 172 min [3]
- **dead2018-06-15.ccm4v.flac16**: source not stated; 19 songs; 170 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [4]
- **deadandcompany2018-06-15.neumann_skm150.sunboy.flac24**: source not stated; 20 songs; 175 min [2]

## Around the show

- Taper stood in the general admission field, just in front of the mixer enclosure, about 15 feet left of center [1]
- Taper positioned roughly 60 feet from the stage, 6 feet high, on the main floor [4]
- Band paid tribute to Brooklyn-born roadie Chris Charucki [6]

## Tapers and lineage

- **deadandcompany2018-06-15.neumann_skm150.sunboy.flac16**: taped by Steven Weld; transferred by Steven Weld; source: Neumann SKM150(AK50's/LC3's/KM100's)>GAKables xlr>Lunatec V2>GAKables xlr>Apogee Mini-Me@24/96>AES/EBU>Sound Devices 722 @24bit/96kHz ~ [1]. Also: Neumann SKM150 mics, taped in the GA field near the mixer, recorded through a Sound Devices 722 at 24-bit/96kHz [1]
- **DeadCo2018-06-15.DeadCo2018-06-15.flac16**: source: AUD [3]. Also: Recorded with Oade M248 mics into an SD722 at 24/48, then processed with iZotope RX and Adobe Audition, and converted to FLAC16 [3]
- **dead2018-06-15.ccm4v.flac16**: taped by Z-Man; source: Schoeps CCM4V's>Lunatec V2>Sound Devices 722 (24/44) [4]
- **deadandcompany2018-06-15.neumann_skm150.sunboy.flac24**: taped by Steven Weld; transferred by Steven Weld; source: Neumann SKM150(AK50's/LC3's/KM100's)>GAKables xlr>Lunatec V2>GAKables xlr>Apogee Mini-Me@24/96>AES/EBU>Sound Devices 722 @24bit/96kHz ~ [2]
